chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not say the Talbiyah until he reached Al-Bayda'.

And a concession has been narrated regarding the permissibility of shortening the Talbiyah in the place where one prays; so if a person acts upon it, there is no harm for him in doing so. He narrated that.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The ritual invocation 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءَ: Al-Bayda, a location near Mecca where pilgrims traditionally begin the Talbiyah
key_terms.تَقْصِيرِ: Shortening (referring to shortening the length of the Talbiyah recitation)
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: A concession or dispensation in religious law

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim begin reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Sunnah of delaying the Talbiyah until reaching Al-Bayda', a location just outside Mecca, reflecting the Prophet’s specific ritual practice. It simultaneously acknowledges the scholarly consensus on *rukhsah* (concession), permitting early Talbiyah to accommodate varying interpretations of the starting point, thereby validating both the strict and flexible approaches in Hajj jurisprudence.
